documents: Detailed inventory in French, valued in euros, dated and signed
Signed certificate that goods will not be resold
Employer letter showing your job abroad and transfer date
French nationals: consulate certificate of change of residence
Proof of French address, e.g. utility bill or lease, max 3 months old
Signed duty-exemption declaration, form Cerfa No. 10070*03
dutyFree: You lived outside the EU for at least 12 months
Belongings and vehicles used by you for at least 6 months
Goods arrive within 12 months of your move to France
restricted: Alcohol pays duty and needs its own inventory with type, value and strength
Tobacco pays duty and is limited
Not allowed: lithium batteries, e-bikes and e-scooters, live plants, dried flowers, fresh fruit
Medicines need Health Ministry approval; firearms need a customs import permit
Cars need the original title in your name (no leased cars) and proof VAT was paid
notes: Keep the goods for at least 12 months after they arrive
If you ship in several loads, list everything on the first inventory
Someone else can handle the customs steps for you with your authorisation

documents: Detailed, valued inventory (separate lists for sea and air)
Employer transfer letter or certificate of change of residence
Original receipts for items bought within the last 2 months
restricted: Vehicles need original registration papers and a non-sale certificate under one month old
notes: Also prepare whatever documents your destination country requires
